subject: hedgehog
pitch: A plump hedgehog out on an autumn evening walk. A dome of spines in chestnut brown with cream tips, a soft fawn face with a pointed, twitchy snout, a shiny black button nose, tiny round ears and bright beady eyes. Little pink paws, and a single red maple leaf stuck on its spines like a trophy.
reasoning:
I'm planning the TypeScript module structure for building a hedgehog model, sizing it realistically at about 25cm long with a domed body shape created through lofted stations, oriented facing +Z.

Now I'm sketching the skeleton: a root joint at the body's center, with a spine chain running through a few vertebrae points from the back to front, plus leg chains, keeping the joint hierarchy moderate in complexity.

Legs need 4 chains (front/back, left/right) with names like hipFL/kneeFL/footFL, using the L/R suffix convention for side. For the body I'm deciding between a loft or ellipsoid dome, and the spines themselves will be individual spike primitives scattered across the back.

For spine placement, I'm scattering hit points across the body surface and generating a spike per hit, using the surface normal at each point as the spike's direction. For the cream-colored tips, instead of trying to gradient-paint a single spike, I'm layering a second shorter cream spike offset further along the normal, positioned by moving the hit point along its local up axis.

I'm also budgeting triangle and part counts: each spike with low side-count sweeps costs roughly 150 triangles, so with around 120 chestnut spines plus 120 cream tips I should stay comfortably under the 60k triangle and 1000 part limits. I'll scatter the spikes from the body loft surface itself, since surface scatter works directly on sweep meshes.

For placement, I need to filter the scattered hits so spines avoid the belly, the front face region where the head attaches, and the leaf spot, using simple normal and position thresholds. For the leaf itself, I'm planning to extrude a small maple-leaf outline from a set of local coordinate points, anchored to a frame near the top of the body.

I'm working out the leaf's orientation so it lies flat across the spines rather than facing forward, computing the right axis vectors for that tangent plane. Then I'm sketching out the body's loft stations—defining width, height, and position at each z-slice from tail to head—to get the overall hedgehog silhouette right.

Now I'm planning the head as its own loft, tapering stations from a wider base near the body down to a small pointed snout tip, with a fawn color and attached to a bone joint for the skeleton rig.

Then I'm setting up the joint hierarchy: a root joint, a spine chain built from a few backbone points, and a neck chain continuing from the spine's end toward the head, working through how parent joints get resolved when no explicit path weights are given so they default to the nearest joint.

For the head, I'm adding an explicit joint parented to the neck tip with its own position and direction, then lofting the head geometry onto that bone. For the legs, I'm planning four chains running from hip to knee to paw, positioning the feet near the floor, and thinking through how to sweep the leg geometry with a fawn color while giving the paws a pink tint, possibly needing a separate part for the paw shape.

Now I'm working out how to bind geometry to the right bone explicitly rather than relying on nearest-joint defaults, since the chain structure makes bone assignment ambiguous for sweeps and capsules. I'm leaning toward passing bone names directly in the sweep options and using a tapered radius array for the legs.

For the head, I'm planning a loft from the body's front toward a pointed snout, with stations shrinking in width and height toward the tip, and placing small black beady eyes embedded into the head surface at roughly symmetric x-offsets near the widest point.

Figuring out eye placement...

Still working out the geometry... the glint sphere's offset keeps pushing it slightly past the eye's radius, so I'm adjusting the normal and lateral offsets to keep the highlight tucked just inside the eye surface.

For ears, I'm thinking I'll use flattened spheres with a scale vector to create a rounded ear shape, positioned via surface hit points on the head near the top sides.

For the nose, I'll place a tiny black sphere at the snout tip using the nearest surface point, and add pink capsule paws. For the leaf on top, I'm computing the surface hit near the top of the body (separate from the spines) and offsetting upward slightly so the leaf sits above the spine tips.

Still working out leaf orientation...

Now thinking about color choices: keeping the leaf a simple red, considering whether the body needs tonal variation with a countershade paint between chestnut back and cream fawn belly, while spines will go chestnut at the base fading to cream tips.

Working out scatter placement for the spines — filtering hits to the upper dome away from the face and belly, then tilting each spine's direction backward by blending the surface normal with a negative z offset so they angle naturally rather than standing straight up.

For the spike geometry itself, I'm nudging the base slightly inward from the surface so it doesn't float, then layering a cream-colored tip segment that follows the same direction vector starting partway up the spine, tapering down with a smaller radius to create the two-tone chestnut-to-cream look.

With roughly 150 spines producing 300 small spike meshes at low polygon counts, the total triangle count stays manageable, and each spike's path and orientation weights come from the surface frame at its base point.

For placement I'm scattering spines across the body using a seeded random generator, minimum distance spacing, and a filter so spines only appear on the upper body surface away from the face and sides, excluding anywhere near the head region. Now I'm figuring out how the body loft itself should inherit bone weighting from its station points.

For the loft I'm passing the spine chain directly as the bone option so the sweep skins smoothly between the back joints rather than relying on nearest-joint lookup from the catmull path. Then I'm laying out the leg chains, assigning hip, knee, and foot joint positions with unique names per leg like hipFL, kneeFL, footFL for the front-left limb.

I'm defining the mirrored back legs with similar hip/knee/foot joint positions shifted along z, using the x-sign convention (positive x = "L" suffix) to keep naming consistent across left/right pairs, then sweeping each leg chain with a small radius and fawn color. For paws I'm adding capsule shapes bound explicitly to the foot joint by name, with a slightly smaller pink radius and rounded caps.

I'm checking leg placement against the body silhouette -- since the hips at x=0.06 sit close to or inside the body's cross-section near the front, I'm nudging leg x-position outward to 0.065 so the legs remain visible beneath the body. Now I'm adjusting the body's station profile (position, width, height at each z-slice from back to front) to get a smoother silhouette.

I'm shaping the head's taper from the body junction toward the snout tip, defining joints for the head and neck parented off the spine chain, and setting up roles like "spine," "leg," and "head" for the rig. I'm placing the eyes, ears, and nose by finding nearest-surface points on the head mesh and offsetting slightly inward for an embedded look, while being careful since the head surface normals near the eye point might land on the side wall rather than the front.

I'm deciding to skip the eye glint detail since I'm unsure it will read well, and confirming the paws and leg bottoms rest exactly at floor level. I'm sketching the leaf outline as a set of tip and curve points with sharp corners at the spike vertices, and considering countershading paint for the body and fawn coloring for the head.

I'm writing the procedural spine-scattering logic: querying scattered hit points across the back of the body with a minimum distance and filtering by position and normal direction, then spawning two-tier spike meshes (a base chestnut spike and a shorter cream tip) at each point with slight random length variation and alternating shades. I'm wiring up the loft calls for body and head with their bone bindings, setting up the joint hierarchy starting from a root "hips" joint that the spine chain and legs attach to by default, and building sphere-based eye geometry attached via stick to the nearest point on the head surface. Finally I'm positioning the leaf attachment point by finding the nearest surface point near the top of the back and offsetting it upward.

I'm now writing the leg construction function parameterized by side and front/back, computing hip-knee-foot joint chains with appropriate names, sweeping a leg mesh along each chain, and adding capsule-shaped paws bound to the foot bones with pink coloring. I'm also refining embed depths for the eyes, nose, and ears so they bulge outward appropriately rather than sinking too far in, and finalizing the leaf's outline points, color, and thickness before assembling everything into the final exported builder function.
